forces.title: Print's shrinking share of the overall Media & Entertainment market
forces.description: The print segment is experiencing a structural decline in its proportional contribution to the Indian Media & Entertainment (M&E) industry. Its share is estimated to decrease from 9.22% in 2026 to 8.00% by 2028. This trend reflects a fundamental shift in consumer habits and advertising spend away from traditional print towards digital platforms. This ongoing re-allocation of resources and attention presents a significant long-term challenge for print publishers.
forces.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

forces.title: Increased FDI limit for Information & Broadcasting, including print media
forces.description: The Indian government has raised the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) limit from 74% to 100% in the Information and Broadcasting sector, which explicitly includes print media. This policy support aims to attract greater foreign capital and expertise into the industry. For print publishers, this could mean enhanced access to investment for technology upgrades, content development, and market expansion, potentially helping to counteract some of the structural headwinds faced by the sector.
forces.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Print's diminishing share within the Indian Media & Entertainment sector
viewpoints.description: The IBEF report indicates a cautious-negative outlook for the print media's relative standing within India's Media & Entertainment (M&E) sector. Print's contribution to the total M&E sector revenue is projected to decline from 9.22% in 2026 to 8.00% by 2028. This structural decline suggests that traditional print publishers are losing market share to other, faster-growing segments, particularly digital media. The decreasing relevance highlights ongoing challenges in attracting advertising revenue and consumer engagement compared to digital platforms.
viewpoints.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India
